entries.name: HTML to PDF (raw HTML)
entries.description: Render a raw HTML document string to a PDF. Returns the PDF as a binary (application/pdf) response. Part of x402-tools, a set of keyless pay-per-call utility APIs settled in USDC via x402.

usage.callShape: POST https://x402.nichospt.net/render with JSON body {"html":"<html>...</html>", "options"?:{format?:"A4"|"Letter", landscape?:bool, margin?}} . x402 payment handshake (USDC on Base). Response is the raw PDF binary, NOT JSON.
usage.outputShape: Binary PDF. Content-Type: application/pdf. Body is the PDF bytes (qa-pay surfaced as base64:JVBERi0xLjQ... i.e. %PDF-1.4 header). No JSON wrapper, no pdf_url — the file itself is the response body.
quirks: Input is a raw HTML STRING in field 'html' (required, maxLength 2,000,000) — NOT a url. This is the key difference from the URL->PDF op.
Output is the PDF binary directly in the response body (Content-Type application/pdf), not a JSON object and not a presigned URL. Save the bytes to disk.
Optional 'options': {format:'A4'|'Letter' (default A4), landscape:bool (default false), margin: CSS-length string or {top,bottom,left,right}}.
Rendered with HeadlessChrome (Skia/PDF) — full CSS/HTML support.
Cheap: $0.005/call, fixed price, keyless (x402 USDC on Base).

entries.name: HTML to PDF (from URL)
entries.description: Render a public remote URL to a PDF. The registered x402-deployer backend is currently BROKEN (unresponsive/timeouts). The same operation is available working+cheaper at x402.nichospt /render-url, recommended as the replacement backend.

usage.callShape: POST {url} with JSON body {"url":"https://example.com"} (x402 USDC on Base). x402-deployer returns {pdf_url} JSON; x402.nichospt /render-url returns the PDF binary directly and accepts an optional 'options' object (format, landscape, margin, waitUntil, viewport).
usage.outputShape: x402-deployer /html-to-pdf: JSON {pdf_url} (CloudConvert presigned S3 URL, X-Amz-Expires=86400 ~24h, not permanent) — UNVERIFIED, endpoint currently times out. x402.nichospt /render-url: binary PDF in response body (application/pdf), like /render — documented from OpenAPI, not pay-verified.
quirks: BROKEN BACKEND: the registered x402-deployer.x402-deployer.workers.dev/html-to-pdf endpoint hangs and times out (HTTP 000 at 30s and 45s, even on an empty body which should return a fast 402 challenge). Origin root returns 200 but this route never responds. qa-pay returned wallet-error 'provider request failed: fetch failed', paid:false — no money was spent and it could not be verified.

RECOMMENDED REPLACEMENT: x402.nichospt /render-url does the same URL->PDF op for $0.005 (vs $0.08) from a provider whose sibling /render endpoint is verified working. Input field 'url' (required, must be public http(s); private/loopback IPs rejected). Optional 'options': {format, landscape, margin, waitUntil: load|domcontentloaded|networkidle0(default)|networkidle2, viewport:{width 320-3840 default 1280, height 240-2160 default 800}}. /render-url returns the PDF binary directly (not a pdf_url).

Input field is 'url' (NOT 'html') — a raw 'html' string is rejected by x402-deployer with 400 'Missing or invalid url field' (and per original notes that 400 still charged $0.08). For raw HTML use the separate /render op instead.
If keeping the x402-deployer backend: pdf_url is a presigned CloudConvert S3 URL valid ~24h — download promptly.

entries.name: PDF Conversion
entries.description: Convert a PDF to Markdown / HTML / JSON / JPG.

usage.outputShape: On success (200): body contains the converted output (markdown/html/json/jpg). Exact key not confirmed because the test PDF host blocked the worker; on error returns body.error (string).
quirks: Input field MUST be named 'pdf_url' (NOT 'url') — wrong name returns 400 {error:"Missing or invalid 'pdf_url' field"} and STILL charges $0.20.

Endpoint server-side fetches the PDF; the PDF host must allow the Cloudflare worker's fetch. W3C/bot-blocked hosts return 403 to the worker -> body.error 'Could not fetch PDF from <url> (403)' and you are charged. Use a PDF on a host that does not bot-block (public S3/GCS bucket, arweave, ipfs gateway).
Endpoint named /pdf-to-markdown but description says it can output Markdown/HTML/JSON/JPG — output format may be selectable via an additional param (not confirmed).
Every call is charged even on 4xx input errors — get the body exactly right before paying.
usage.guide: POST to https://x402-deployer.x402-deployer.workers.dev/pdf-to-markdown with JSON body {"pdf_url":"<url-to-a-publicly-fetchable-pdf>"} and pay $0.20 USDC on Base via x402. The field MUST be 'pdf_url' (using 'url' returns a 400 but still charges). The server fetches the PDF itself, so the URL must point to a host that allows automated/worker fetches (avoid bot-blocked hosts like w3.org, which return 403). Read the converted markdown from the 2xx response body; on failure read body.error.

entries.name: MakesPDF Markdown to PDF
entries.description: Convert GitHub-Flavoured Markdown to a tagged, accessible PDF (PDF/UA-1 + PDF/A-2A dual-compliant). Sub-second, no AI call. Cheapest path when you already have document text.

usage.callShape: POST https://makespdf.com/api/v1/markdown with JSON body {markdown: string, options?: object}. Only `markdown` is required. `options` accepts pageSize (e.g. A4), fontFamily, fontSize, margins, title, theme.

inputExample.markdown:
# Hello World

Some **bold** text and a list:

- one
- two

usage.outputShape: Raw binary PDF (Content-Type: application/pdf). Via x402/paid_fetch the body is returned as a 'base64:<base64-of-PDF-bytes>' string — strip the 'base64:' prefix and base64-decode to get the PDF (starts with %PDF-1.7). Response headers carry x-pages (page count) and x-render-ms (render latency); options.title sets the content-disposition filename.
quirks: x402 payment bypasses the normal Bearer-token requirement — no API key needed for the paid call.
Response is RAW BINARY PDF, not JSON. paid_fetch/qa-pay surface it as a 'base64:...' string — strip the prefix and base64-decode to get PDF bytes (magic %PDF-1.7).
Field is `markdown` (GFM source), not `text` or `content`. `options` is a flat object (pageSize, fontFamily, fontSize, margins, title, theme).

Same operation is also reachable at the anonymous alias POST /api/v1/md (rate-limited 60/hour, 200/day, 20 pages) when the operator enables promo:md_anonymous_enabled — but the registry/x402 path uses /api/v1/markdown.
x-pages and x-render-ms headers report page count and render latency; options.title sets the download filename.

entries.name: MakesPDF Template Render
entries.description: Generate a PDF from structured data with no source document — supply data plus a curated-library template id (or inline builder DSL). Output is a tagged, accessible PDF/UA-1 + PDF/A-2A document. Use for branded layouts like invoices, certificates, reports.

usage.callShape: POST https://makespdf.com/api/v1/render with JSON body {templateId: string, data: object} OR {dsl: string, data: object}. templateId and dsl are mutually exclusive — supply exactly one. `data` holds the template variables.
usage.outputShape: Raw binary PDF (Content-Type: application/pdf). Via x402/paid_fetch returned as 'base64:<base64-of-PDF-bytes>' — strip the prefix and decode (starts with %PDF-1.7). Same x-pages / x-render-ms headers as the markdown endpoint.
quirks: x402 payment bypasses the normal Bearer-token requirement — no API key needed for the paid call.
Response is RAW BINARY PDF, not JSON — surfaced as a 'base64:...' string by paid_fetch/qa-pay; strip prefix and base64-decode.

`templateId` and `dsl` are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE — pass exactly one. templateId is the simplest path; browse valid ids at GET /api/v1/templates?owner=library (free). Verified id: invoice-classic. Other library ids: certificate-formal, certificate-modern, invoice-compact, invoice-modern.
Template variables go in the `data` object (not top-level). invoice-classic tolerates partial data; other templates may expect specific fields.
Costs $0.02 (double the /markdown endpoint at $0.01).
